Write clean, PEP8 compliant Python code. Use meaningful variable names and include docstrings for functions and classes. Avoid using global variables and ensure that your code is modular and reusable.
Always include type hints in functions signatures to improve code readability and maintainability. Use list comprehensions and generator expressions where appropriate to make your code more concise and efficient. Additionally, handle exceptions gracefully and provide informative error messages to help with debugging.
Prioritize and modularity for academic portfolio projects, ensuring that each function and class has a single responsibility. This will make your code easier to test and maintain. When working on collaborative projects, follow the established coding conventions and style guides to ensure consistency across the codebase.
